Description: When a policy earns a dividend, that dividend counts toward what the policyholder has put into the contract, which is what cost basis is built from. We had already brought over total premiums paid, but the dividend side was missing completely — QLAdmin's dividend history screen was blank for every policy, even though LifePRO shows these policies earned $1,889,445.44 in dividends across 593 policies. Eric asked for the dividend total to come over the same way we handled premium history.
Notes: Fixed in v58.36. The accounting records only go back to 2018 but these policies have paid dividends for decades, so we did the same two-part approach used for premiums: load the 2,500 real dividend payments we have from 2018 on ($401,443.32), then add one catch-up line per policy dated 12/31/2017 for everything before that ($1,473,854.50). Result: 586 policies now have dividend history where there was none, and every one of the 579 policies we converted matches the LifePRO lifetime total to the penny. That is $1,875,297.82 of $1,889,445.44, or 99.25%. Nothing already in the table was disturbed. 14 policies are held back for Eric rather than guessed at: 7 use a dividend option called Reduce Loan that QLAdmin has no category for ($16,514.26), 4 have a dividend total but no option recorded ($163.96), and 3 already have more in the recent records than LifePRO reports as their lifetime total. Another $18,719.96 sits on rider records and was left out to match how premiums were handled. Also caught and fixed a bug before delivery where a dividend posted on both sides of an accounting entry was being counted twice — worth noting because the dollar totals still balanced and only a row-level duplicate check found it.
